text: For an input field placed at its front focal plane, what mathematical operation does a thin converging lens perform on that field at the back focal plane?
choices: It computes the 2D spatial autocorrelation of the input field
It computes the spatial gradient (derivative) of the input field
It computes the exact 2D spatial Fourier transform of the input field
It convolves the input with a fixed Gaussian point-spread function
explanation: A lens's quadratic phase exactly cancels the quadratic phase of the Fraunhofer diffraction integral, so the back-focal-plane field is the exact 2D Fourier transform of the front-focal-plane field, with spatial frequencies f_x = x'/(lambda*f). Autocorrelation and convolution are properties of a full 4f system, not of a single lens, and a lens does not differentiate the field.
